A1.justification: Both complete 35-page PDFs describe the same ART makeup-transfer work and include supplementary Sections A–D. Text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison; differences are confined to the arXiv stamp and one Figure 2 thumbnail.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark experiments, ablations, qualitative results and a user study with 864 ratings from 21 participants, including additional results in the supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark experiments, ablations, qualitative results and user-study outcomes in the main paper and supplement.

M1.justification: The two-stage ART procedure, auxiliary makeup remover, differentiable refinement cycle, controlled-noise bottleneck, losses and inference procedure are unchanged. The Figure 2 thumbnail correction does not change the specified method.

E1.justification: Both versions use MT, LADN, MT-Wild and MF2K, with the same resolution coverage and supplementary cross-domain examples involving anime characters and 3D avatars.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in all corresponding experiments, including PSGAN, EleGANt, MAD, SHMT, StableMakeup, Nano Banana Pro and GPT Image 1.5 in Table 1.

E3.justification: Training settings, metrics, evaluation procedures and user-study design are identical. Both retain the standard 100-pair evaluations and supplementary 1,000-pair LADN evaluation.

E4.justification: The training-stage, noise-level, structural-regularization, pseudo-target-source and unpaired-data ablations are unchanged, as are the makeup-removal robustness tests, metric analyses and failure cases.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical. No repeated-run or seed information, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings and experimental qualitative comparisons are unchanged throughout the main paper and supplement. The replacement thumbnail in Figure 2 reuses the Nano Banana Pro output already displayed in Figure 1, adding no new result.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, flow-matching and refinement objectives, wavelet-loss formulation and supplementary mathematical descriptions are identical. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about breaking the pseudo-target ceiling, introducing MF2K and achieving high-fidelity makeup transfer with identity preservation.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the refinement mechanism, ablation findings and evaluation metrics are unchanged. Section 4.6 and supplementary Section D retain the same illumination and reflectance limitation.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, hardware and computational costs, data-curation instructions, synthesis and evaluation prompts, and the project link are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the positioning relative to weak supervision and pseudo-target methods, and all 55 references are unchanged.

P1.justification: The marginal arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 30 June 2026 to v2 dated 31 July 2026. Manuscript wording, author information, terminology and section structure are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: In Figure 2, v1 duplicates the source portrait in the position labeled 'pseudo target'; v2 replaces it with the makeup-bearing Nano Banana Pro output already shown in Figure 1. The surrounding diagram, captions, tables and remaining figures are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Correcting Figure 2 makes the pseudo-target illustration consistent with the described training procedure: the synthetic target now shows applied makeup instead of duplicating the source image. This is a limited improvement in explanatory accuracy; the scientific content, empirical evidence and appendices remain unchanged.
